text:
tanya: heads up — seeing a sharp p99 token latency spike out of FRA pop starting ~09:10 UTC. hosted customers degraded, throughput down ~30%. logs show kernel fallback churn and kv-cache miss rate jump. :eyes:

devon: can you paste the console traces / top graphs? any DNS/peering alerts?

tanya: https://console.redwood/ops/trace/1912345678 — the trace shows long server-side queuing and a bunch of requests hitting the fallback kernel selector. copying a quick snippet:

```
p99_token_latency_ms: 256 -> 920
throughput_rps: 1200 -> 780
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.78 -> 0.46
kernel_selector: avx512_opt -> fallback_scalar -> avx512_opt (oscillating)
cpu_steal_pct_host: 4.2% -> 18.7%
```
ingrid: CPU steal jump suggests noisy neighbor on the host or hypervisor scheduling. fallback kernel has ~3x slower per-token perf which explains p99. KV cache miss spike could be from eviction churn if requests slowed and windows overlap more.

miguel: which ISP / provider for FRA? any peering events?

tanya: DE-ISP-1 egress. no BGP flaps in our monitoring but provider reports elevated queueing on some links. ops-bot: created ticket NET-8721 with provider.

runtime-bot: alert: kernel-selector-frequency high; fallback-switches=46 in last 10m; auto-routing engaged (latency_policy: prefer-region)

devon: can we capture a perf profile on one affected host and dump kernel selector debug? also get kv cache stats per-worker.

ingrid: run `sudo perf record -a -g -F 99 -o /tmp/perf_fra.data -- sleep 30` on the worker and `rd-runtime --dump-kv-stats` for kv metrics. MIGUEL do you have short windows to collect?

miguel: grabbing profiles now. also enabling selector debug via `RUNTIME_KS_DEBUG=1` on canaries. will stream logs to #eng-runtime.

miguel: paste from perf (flame snippet):

```
Top symbols: 1) runtime::attn::kv_lookup (35%) 2) runtime::kernels::scalar_loop (27%) 3) kernel_selector::decide (8%) 4) system_sched_schedule (6%)
```

devon: that scalar_loop is the fallback kernel — matches the slower kernel. kernel_selector seems to be flipping because latency spikes cause it to think avx512 paths are regressing. maybe the selector's hysteresis is too tight under noisy-host conditions.

tanya: kv stats from worker-13:

```
worker: worker-13
active_batches: 18
avg_batch_size: 4.1
kv_cache_entries: 92k -> 68k (during spike)
kv_evictions_per_min: 1500 -> 6400
kv_window_hits: 0.60 -> 0.33
```
ingrid: eviction rate surge confirms thrash. eviction_threshold configured to 80k in FRA pool; looks like eviction logic kicked in earlier because of sudden memory pressure (host-level reclaim due to steal?). if the kernel flips to fallback, processing slows, inflight windows increase -> kv pressure -> more evictions -> more misses -> more work -> vicious cycle.

devon: short term mitigations: 1) pin kernel selector to avx512_opt for canary hosts in FRA (force preferred kernel) 2) lower avg batch size (max_batch=8 -> 4) to reduce per-request latency 3) bump kv_cache_threshold to 120k and raise eviction backoff window.

miguel: applied canary changes: pinned kernel on 3 canaries, adjusted batching config on routing rule fra-pop to prefer smaller batches. monitoring now. ops-bot: routing change pushed — 4% of traffic diverted to AMS as additional safety.

runtime-bot: canary metrics (5m after mitigation): p95_token_latency down 2.1x on pinned hosts, kv hitrate improving on canaries.

tanya: provider reported they cleared queueing on egress link ~09:40 UTC. but we still need to harden selector and kv eviction logic to avoid recurrence.

ingrid: action items I propose:
- increase selector hysteresis: require 3 consecutive samples before switching (current=1)
- prefer stable kernel under high steal: add metric cpu_steal_pct to selector decision with threshold 10%
- increase kv_cache_soft_limit and add eviction backoff when kernel is in fallback mode
- add a temporary routing policy that detects kernel-fallback oscillation and routes to another POP automatically
devon: agree. small follow-ups: add unit tests for kernel selector with simulated steal; add end-to-end integration test where kv miss rate artificially increased and ensure we don't oscillate.

miguel: I started a PR for selector hysteresis: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4389 (draft) — includes steal gating and a simple exponential backoff for switches.

tanya: created incident INC-2026-FRA-LAT with summary + timeline + mitigations. assigned to eng-runtime + infra + network.

devon: quick note for postmortem: root cause is interplay of provider-side queueing (causing CPU steal-ish behavior on hosts), kernel selector that is too sensitive, and kv cache eviction thresholds tuned for steady-state but not transient slow-downs. Not a single root cause but a cascade.

ingrid: timeline entry: 09:10 spike begins -> 09:18 kernel selector starts oscillation -> 09:25 kv eviction surge -> 09:33 canary mitigations applied -> 09:40 provider clears queueing -> 09:50 p99 returns to baseline after config rollouts.

miguel: monitoring now shows p99 stabilized ~110ms (pre-incident baseline ~95ms). kv hitrate back to 0.77. ops-bot: updated NET-8721 status to provider-acknowledged.
tanya: thanks all. next steps: merge PR after review, schedule a runtime release with selector changes, and run a chaos test to simulate host steal + high kv pressure. I'll write the postmortem template and link the metrics/graphs. :white_check_mark:
